paper_metadata.title: DISCRETE-TIME QUANTUM WALK OF A BOSE-EINSTEIN CONDENSATE IN MOMENTUM SPACE

summary: This dissertation reports a discrete-time quantum walk of a Bose-Einstein condensate of ultracold 87Rb atoms in momentum space, using microwave coin pulses and a resonant quantum ratchet shift operator. The paper demonstrates standard walks, biased walks, reversals, and quantum-to-classical transition behavior over up to 20 steps, with example parameters including kicking strengths |k| = 1.2, 1.45, and 1.8, biased coin probability 0.7, and spontaneous-emission noise around 0.5% per kick per atom.

experiments.description: Discrete-time quantum walk of a Bose-Einstein condensate in momentum space using ultracold 87Rb atoms, with a microwave coin toss and a resonant quantum ratchet shift operator; includes standard walks, steered walks, walk reversal, and quantum-to-classical transition studies.

algorithm.variant: discrete-time quantum walk in momentum space with microwave coin and AOKR-based quantum ratchet shift

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Two internal hyperfine states of 87Rb serve as the coin; momentum classes of the atoms form the walk space. Each step applies a microwave coin operator followed by a unitary momentum shift via a quantum ratchet.

problem_instance.description: Quantum walk implemented on a Bose-Einstein condensate of ultracold rubidium-87 atoms in momentum space.

dataset_specification.description: 87Rb BEC prepared via MOT, dipole trap, and evaporative cooling; momentum-space walk measured after time-of-flight imaging

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: BEC created, released from dipole trap, subjected to walk perturbations, then given ~10 ms time of flight; repump pulse applied before imaging
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of experimental momentum distributions and mean energy with simulations/theory across different step counts and parameter settings

noise_model.noise_type: experimental imperfections including thermal cloud, quasimomentum spread, spontaneous emission, and coin-phase randomness

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: BEC preparation, momentum-space initialization, parameter tuning of microwave and kicking pulses
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Time-of-flight absorption imaging and extraction of momentum distributions/mean energy

speedup_claims.conditions: The paper discusses quantum walks as promising for quantum algorithms, but this specific experiment is an analog atomic-physics implementation and does not report an asymptotic computational speedup.
speedup_claims.caveats: No gate-based quantum-computing speedup is demonstrated; results concern physical walk dynamics, not algorithmic runtime.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Not applicable: the paper studies physical quantum-walk dynamics in a BEC, not a computational benchmark with a classical runtime comparison on a problem instance.
limiting_factors: No algorithmic speedup benchmark is reported

notes: Hardware inferred as real_qpu_neutral_atom because the experiment is performed on ultracold 87Rb atoms in a laboratory BEC setup, not on a digital gate-based quantum processor; however, this is not a gate-based quantum-computing experiment in the thesis scope.
